reuse.why: Extends the existing single weekend-rule definition (applyWeekendRule / applyWeekendRuleToDay / getDateWithSkippedWeekend) and RSchedule instead of adding a parallel holiday mechanism.

duplication.why: No logic is copied, but every RSchedule construction site (rule-utils, find-schedules, two in schedules/app) now repeats the rrules+exdates pairing, and holidays is threaded by hand through each applyWeekendRule call.

placement.why: Move and skip logic live in shared/schedules.ts next to the existing weekend rule and recurConfigToRSchedule; call sites only pass config data.

scope.why: Limited to the holiday feature: type field, shared rule, call-site threading, a focused test and a release note.

maintainability.why: The move rule is cleanly generalised via isOffDay, but the daily-skip half is split between recurConfigToRSchedule (weekends) and a separate recurConfigToExdates every caller must remember to add, and getMaxWeekendShift is a coarse bound.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All move decisions still go through applyWeekendRule/getDateWithSkippedWeekend in shared/schedules.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: Nothing is copied; the repeated `new RSchedule({ rrules: recurConfigToRSchedule(config), exdates: recurConfigToExdates(config) })` at four sites is repetition of a call pair, not disguised logic.

one_place.where: Holiday moves land in getDateWithSkippedWeekend (isOffDay) used via applyWeekendRule by every path; daily holiday skipping lands in recurConfigToExdates in shared/schedules.ts, which all four RSchedule sites call, though separately from the weekend skip in recurConfigToRSchedule.
